summary: Construction, freight trucking and small-manufacturer supply chains score highest: money is visibly stuck in paperwork, buyers already pay for basic software, and AI products for these exact jobs are rare.

candidates.name: Construction & real estate
candidates.reason: Large, visible money at stake (stuck bills, staged loan releases), compliance that recurs every quarter, and few AI products beyond basic site apps.
candidates.one_liner: Contractors, developers and the lenders who fund them; paper bills, stage inspections, RERA filings.

signals.text: Housing lenders release loans in stages after a site inspection
Hundreds of open 'billing engineer' roles at contractors
Developers file quarterly progress on state RERA portals

candidates.name: Freight trucking & transport
candidates.reason: Every trip already has a digital trail (e-way bill, FASTag), yet payment waits on a paper proof of delivery. Owners feel cash-flow pain weekly.
candidates.one_liner: Small fleet owners and transporters; paper PODs and lorry receipts, slow payments.

signals.text: E-way bills create a digital record for most goods movements
Transporters' Hindi YouTube channels discuss payment delays after delivery
ONDC runs a logistics network open to new providers

candidates.name: MSME manufacturing (engineering & auto components)
candidates.reason: Owners already pay for Tally and some ERP, quoting and OEM quality documents eat engineers' time, and few tools target the small supplier.
candidates.one_liner: Job shops and tier-2/3 suppliers; manual quoting, quality paperwork for OEMs.

signals.text: Auto-component suppliers must submit quality documentation to OEMs
Buyers post RFQs with drawings that suppliers answer by hand
Many 'costing / estimation engineer' openings at small manufacturers

candidates.name: CA & tax practices
candidates.reason: Strong fit for AI but crowded with GST and accounting tools; the clearest gaps are features, not companies.

candidates.name: Textiles & garments (Surat, Tiruppur)
candidates.reason: Real pain in job-work tracking, but buyers are price-sensitive and run on long credit; no clear trigger now.

candidates.name: Jewellery retail & manufacturing
candidates.reason: Hallmarking created new paperwork, but much of it is already handled by government-approved centres.

candidates.name: Pharma distribution & chemists
candidates.reason: Well served by Marg ERP and several funded B2B platforms; thin margins cap software spend.

candidates.name: Hospitals & diagnostic centres (Tier 2)
candidates.reason: Pain is real but clinical and data rules slow sales; funded players already target this segment.

candidates.name: Independent hotels & restaurants
candidates.reason: Petpooja and aggregator tools dominate; switching is cheap but margins are thin.

candidates.name: Schools & coaching institutes
candidates.reason: Fees and attendance software is crowded; AI tutoring is a B2C play outside this playbook.

candidates.name: Kirana & general trade
candidates.reason: Crowded: free tools from Khatabook, Jio and FMCG distributors set the price at zero.

candidates.name: Agriculture & FPOs
candidates.reason: Low willingness to pay; most buying flows through government schemes with long cycles.

candidates.name: Dairy cooperatives
candidates.reason: Buying decisions sit with cooperative boards and state federations; slow sales.

candidates.name: Real estate brokerage
candidates.reason: Brokers spend on listings portals, not workflow tools; pain is lead quality, which portals own.

candidates.name: State and municipal departments
candidates.reason: Hits a kill criterion: only route is long tenders with no pilot path.
